paragraphs: The XF 5.0 V8 uses the AJ133 engine family, a 5.0-litre V8 petrol unit that replaced the earlier 4.2-litre AJ34 in the X250 generation from around 2011. The naturally aspirated AJ133 powered the standard XF V8, while the supercharged AJ133S — producing significantly more power — powered the XFR flagship. Both share the same 5.0-litre V8 architecture and the same timing chain tensioner design, which is the key known wear point across this engine family.
about.boldParagraph: The XF 5.0 V8 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 5.0-litre naturally aspirated V8 fitted to the XF V8 from around 2011 to 2015 (X250). Known for the timing chain tensioner design flaw — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, tensioners, guides, and water pump as standard on every AJ133 rebuild.

A 5.0-litre supercharged V8 fitted to the XFR from around 2011 to 2015 (X250). Shares the same AJ133 architecture and timing chain tensioner pattern as the naturally aspirated version. We replace the timing chain, tensioners, guides, and water pump as standard on every AJ133S rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The XF 5.0 V8 uses the AJ133 engine family across its X250 generation run. While the naturally aspirated and supercharged versions share the same core architecture, they have different ancillaries, cooling requirements, and ECU mapping.
